quote: The Caenomanians complained of this to the senate at Rome, and were by them referred to the consul Aemilius
notes: Disarmed Cenomani appeal to the senate against the praetor Furius, who is ordered to restore their arms and quit the province (livy:en:39:3).

quote: In consequence of this inquiry, twelve thousand Latins returned home; as the multitude of foreigners even then burdened the city.
notes: Latin confederate envoys protest migration of their citizens to Rome; praetorian inquiry compels twelve thousand Latins to return home (livy:en:39:3).

quote: Marcus Abutius, a tribune of the commons, gave notice, that, if any thing were determined on that subject before the arrival of Marcus Aemilius, he would enter his protest
notes: Tribune Abutius, acting for the absent consul Aemilius, threatens veto of Fulvius' triumph until his colleague Gracchus shames him into withdrawing and the triumph is voted (quote at livy:en:39:4; resolution in 39:5).

quote: The reason of his deferring his triumph so long was, to avoid standing a trial under the Petillian law
notes: Manlius Vulso delays his Asian triumph to escape prosecution under the Petillian law amid the fallout of Lucius Scipio's condemnation (livy:en:39:6).

quote: The following year diverted Spurius Postumius Albinus and Quintus Marcius Philippus, from the care of armies, and wars, and provinces, to the punishing of an intestine conspiracy.
notes: The Bacchanalian cult spreading from Etruria is framed as an intestine conspiracy and both consuls are assigned the inquisition into clandestine meetings (livy:en:39:8).

quote: Their number was exceedingly great now, almost a second state in themselves, and among them were many men and women of noble families.
notes: The freedwoman informer Hispala, under consular promise of protection, discloses the cult's scale and crimes, describing it as almost a second state (quote at livy:en:39:13; testimony begins 39:12).

quote: They then commit to the consuls the holding an inquiry, out of the common course, concerning the Bacchanals and their nocturnal orgies.
notes: Senate erects an extraordinary inquisition with informer rewards, Italy-wide proclamation, night watches, and protection for Aebutius and Fecenia - a full accusation apparatus (livy:en:39:14).

quote: Above seven thousand men and women are said to have taken the oath of the association.
notes: After the consular edict terror spreads through Italy; fugitives are seized at the gates, suicides follow, and the chief priests of the sect confess (livy:en:39:17).

quote: A greater number were executed than thrown into prison; indeed, the multitude of men and women who suffered in both ways, was very considerable.
notes: Those guilty of debauchery, murder, or fraud under the Bacchanalian oath are put to death en masse, condemned women handed to relations for private execution (livy:en:39:18).

quote: the senate passed a decree, that no Bacchanalian rites should be celebrated in Rome or in Italy
notes: The senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus permanently bans the rites save by senatorial licence with no more than five worshippers, no common fund, and no priest (livy:en:39:18).

quote: the city quaestors should give to each of them, out of the public treasury, one hundred thousand asses
notes: Senate and commons vote money, military exemption for Aebutius, and unprecedented legal privileges for the freedwoman Fecenia, institutionalizing the informer-reward machinery (livy:en:39:19).

quote: he had found two colonies deserted, Sipontum on the upper sea, and Buxentum on the lower
notes: On the consul's report of two deserted colonies, the senate appoints commissioners to conduct new settlers to Sipontum and Buxentum (livy:en:39:23).

quote: During that year there was a formidable insurrection of the slaves in Apulia.
notes: A slave and shepherd conspiracy infesting roads and pastures around Tarentum is crushed by the praetor, who condemns some seven thousand (livy:en:39:29).

quote: Claudius, the consul, unattended by his lictors, canvassed with his brother through all parts of the forum
notes: Consul Appius Claudius flouts propriety by canvassing for his brother; tribunician contentions repeatedly interrupt the election before Publius Claudius wins against expectation (livy:en:39:32).

quote: The former threatened, if the senate voted for bringing home the armies, to protest against their decree
notes: Tribunes and consuls line up on both sides over discharging the Spanish armies, trading veto threats until a compromise decree on recruitment and discharge passes (livy:en:39:38).

quote: The senate therefore gave their judgment, that the present number of praetors was sufficient
notes: The curule aedile elect Fulvius Flaccus obstinately stands for a vacant praetorship against the consul and senate, who finally abandon the by-election altogether (livy:en:39:39).

quote: in spite of the opposition made by the nobility, they not only made Marcus Porcius censor, but gave him for his colleague Lucius Valerius Flaccus
notes: The combined nobility fails to block Cato, who campaigns on menaces of a severe censorship and carries Valerius Flaccus in with him (quote at livy:en:39:41; candidacies in 39:40).

quote: If we are to credit Valerius Antias, he condemned about two thousand men.
notes: The praetor Naevius is detained four months by inquisitions into poisonings held through the corporate towns, with some two thousand condemned per Antias (livy:en:39:41).

quote: punished numerous conspiracies of the peasants, and, with great care, finished the remainder of the inquiries concerning the Bacchanalians
notes: The praetor of Tarentum completes the residual Bacchanalian inquisitions, executing some fugitives from bail and remanding others to prison at Rome (livy:en:39:41).

quote: they expelled seven from the senate, one of them a man of consular rank, highly distinguished by nobility of birth and honourable employments
notes: Cato's censorial review expels seven senators, above all the consular Lucius Quinctius Flamininus for killing a Gaul at dinner to amuse his favourite (quote at livy:en:39:42; Antias variant in 39:43).

quote: In the review of the knights, Lucius Scipio Asiaticus was degraded.
notes: In the equestrian review the censors strip Lucius Scipio Asiaticus of his horse, extending Cato's campaign against the Scipionic circle (livy:en:39:44).

quote: They farmed out the several branches of the revenue at the highest prices, and bargained with the contractors for the performance of the public services on the lowest terms.
notes: Cato's censorship taxes luxury tenfold, reclaims public water and ground, builds the Basilica Porcia, and defies senate revocation of the tax-farming contracts by re-letting them (livy:en:39:44).

quote: two colonies were established, Potentia in Picenum, and Pisaurum in the Gallic territory. Six acres were given to each settler.
notes: Citizen colonies are planted at Potentia and Pisaurum with six acres per settler under a single board of commissioners (livy:en:39:44).

quote: He gave a charge to Onomastus, who had the command of the sea-coast, to put to death the leaders of the opposite party.
notes: Macedonian polity: ordered to free Maronea, Philip instead has the pro-Roman leaders massacred and poisons Cassander rather than surrender him to senatorial examination (livy:en:39:34).

quote: as every thing was directed by passion, not by reason, they were condemned to die
notes: Achaean polity: the general council, inflamed against the restored Spartan exiles Areus and Alcibiades for their embassy to Rome, condemns them to death (livy:en:39:35).

quote: Nothing more was done, only the sentence lately passed on Areus and Alcibiades was reversed.
notes: Achaean polity: after Lycortas' defiant defence of Achaean sovereignty, Appius Claudius' veiled threat compels reversal of the death sentence on the Spartan appellants to Rome (livy:en:39:37).

quote: disturbances still subsisted, in consequence of the old quarrels, and Messene had revolted from the Achaean confederacy
notes: Greek polity: Messene secedes from the Achaean confederacy, a revolt ultimately crushed and reversed after war (quote at livy:en:39:48; outcome in 39:50).

quote: The party that were more eager for his immediate execution, at length prevailed, and a person was sent to him with poison.
notes: Messenian polity: the captured Achaean praetor Philopoemen is imprisoned in the public treasury and poisoned by the revolt's leaders against popular sentiment; Messene later surrenders the guilty (quote at livy:en:39:50; capture in 39:49).

quote: The present generation have sent an ambassador, of consular rank, to persuade Prusias villanously to murder his guest.
notes: Roman political side of Hannibal's death: Flamininus' embassy to Prusias precipitates the guarding of Hannibal's house and his suicide by poison (livy:en:39:51).

quote: though neither banished nor condemned, yet under prosecution, and summoned as an absent criminal to a trial, at which he did not appear, passed sentence of voluntary exile
notes: Livy dates Scipio Africanus' death from his prosecution by the tribune Naevius: still under charge, he dies in self-imposed exile refusing burial at Rome (livy:en:39:52).

quote: Fear tortured Perseus, lest his age alone might not sufficiently secure his interest, his brother having the advantage of him in every other particular
notes: Macedonian polity: Demetrius' Roman favour breeds envy in Perseus and suspicion in Philip, the dynastic intrigue that will destroy Demetrius (quote at livy:en:39:53; senate's honouring of Demetrius in 39:47-48).

quote: They sent ambassadors to Rome to complain of those proceedings, who being introduced to an audience of the senate
notes: Disarmed Gallic settlers appeal to the senate, which orders their property restored provided they recross the Alps and warns the Gallic states (livy:en:39:54).

quote: In the same year, colonies of Roman citizens were led out to Mutina and Parma.
notes: The senate debates Latin versus citizen status for Aquileia, deciding for a Latin colony, while citizen colonies go out to Mutina, Parma, and Saturnia (livy:en:39:55).
